question: Is the following claim true? The speed of sound in dry air at 20 °C is about 443 metres per second.
source: author-written for this project; verified by the author

claims.text: The claim that sound speed in dry air at 20 °C is about 443 m/s is false.
The actual speed of sound in dry air at 20 °C is about 343 m/s.
The empirical formula v ≈ 331.3 + 0.606·T gives about 343 m/s at 20 °C.
The speed of sound in air at 0 °C is about 331 m/s and rises about 0.6 m/s per degree, giving about 343 m/s at 20 °C.
The claimed value is about 100 m/s (roughly 29%) too high, far beyond rounding or measurement uncertainty.
The 443 figure could be a simple transcription error of 343.
Nothing in the physics supports a value of 443 m/s for air at 20 °C.
Sound travels faster in denser or hotter media, so one might guess a higher value, but this does not justify 443 m/s.
Air at 20 °C does not reach 443 m/s under any standard conditions.
